summary: Official Windows service control for Windows Search (WSearch). Microsoft documents the service name, start-mode baseline, feature behavior, and says it is OK to disable in the service guidance used here. The app disables the service by setting its start mode to Disabled.

setting.name: Windows Search Service
setting.casual_explanation: Windows Search builds and maintains an index so Start and Explorer can return indexed results without a full content crawl. Disabling it reduces indexing activity, but it also removes the indexed search experience.
setting.why_people_change_it: People disable it when they do not use Windows indexing, prefer third-party search tools, or want to reduce indexing-related background work.
setting.tradeoffs_overview: Turning off the service can reduce indexing work, but Windows Search features lose indexed results and some experiences can become slower or unavailable.
setting.professional_notes: Microsoft's Windows IoT Enterprise service guidance lists Windows Search `(WSearch)` with a documented start mode baseline and marks it `OK to disable`. Microsoft also documents the Windows Search indexing process and confirms the feature area and its role in indexed search results. The current app disables `WSearch` through a service start-mode tweak.

evidence.title: QGA service inspection receipt for WSearch
evidence.summary: A 2026-05-07 non-mutating QGA service inspection captured `sc qc WSearch`, the backing `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\WSearch` / `Start` value, and PowerShell `Win32_Service`/`Get-Service` output. The guest confirmed exact service identity `WSearch`, display name `Windows Search`, current VM start mode `Auto` / `Automatic`, service state `Running`, and `Start` DWORD `0x2` without mutating the service. This supersedes the earlier ETW artifact-upload blocker for this service-control lane; Microsoft guidance remains the default and disable-support authority.

evidence.title: KVM ETW stage receipt for WSearch backing registry key
evidence.summary: A bounded 2026-04-24 ETW retry for the WSearch backing registry key reached artifact-upload and only retained a stage receipt before the hard timeout fired.

evidence.title: Guest Ghidra launch receipt for WSearch
evidence.summary: A bounded 2026-04-24 guest string-xref retry for `WSearch` failed in `ensure-admin-shell` before any Ghidra bundle reached the host.

decision.why: Microsoft documents the WSearch service name, its Manual baseline, its search-indexing behavior, and explicitly marks it OK to disable in the service guidance used here. The app's service-start-mode action matches that documented control surface cleanly.

source_enrichment.notes: Disable Windows Search in the power provider remains an official-doc and repo-code lane, not a source-mirror-backed runtime record. A bounded 2026-04-24 KVM ETW retry for the backing WSearch registry key only produced a host-visible stage receipt before the hard 90 second timeout fired, and the paired guest Ghidra retry for `WSearch` failed in `ensure-admin-shell` before any xref bundle reached the host. A 2026-05-07 non-mutating QGA service inspection superseded the earlier ETW artifact-upload blocker for `WSearch` by confirming the exact SCM service identity, current VM start mode, service state, and backing `Start` DWORD without changing the service.
